'''Legal Lexicon''' is the legal-language and sources-of-authority surface of the [[SoapBox]] civic ecosystem, published at lexicon.soapbox.community. Its full title is ''Legal Lexicon & Sources of Authority''. It explains the words the law uses and, separately, which texts actually carry legal weight — as reference, not as legal advice.

== What it covers ==
* '''Legal dictionaries vs. the law''' — why a dictionary definition and a controlling legal definition are not the same thing.
* '''Founding-era meaning''' — how the original public meaning of a term is recovered and used.
* '''American vs. British common law''' — where the two diverge and why it matters to a U.S. reader.
* '''Sources of authority''' — the distinction between binding and merely persuasive authority.
* '''An American legal lexicon''' — a glossary of terms with a plain gloss and a source.

== Editorial rule ==
Consistent with the rest of the [[SoapBox Law]] surface, the material is sourced and descriptive — ''facts, not verdicts'' — and is not legal advice.
